item.title: Objects That Inspire: Four Indian Creatives Tell Us About What Inspires Them
item.description: What sparks creativity? A glass sphinx, a scent trail, a Basquiat Bearbrick, a kitchen door full of memories. Four Indian creatives reveal the objects that inspire and shape their practice.

item.title: 'Across' Brings An Authentic & Constantly Evolving Taste Of The Himalayas To Kala Ghoda
item.description: Inside Across: The Himalayan Restaurant Bringing Mountain Memory To Mumbai At Across, chefs Viraaf Patel and Prakriti Lama Patel reinterpret Himalayan food traditions through memory, research, and deeply personal roots in the region.

item.title: Delhi Exhibition 'Bitter Nectar' Maps Climate Change Through Everyday Food Systems
item.description: Sustaina India 3, Bitter Nectar Examines Climate Change Through India’s Food Systems The exhibition collectively places environmental knowledge within bodily experience and inherited responsibility.

item.title: Short Film 'That Perfect Day' Unpacks The Intersection Of Class, Childhood, & Paternal Love
item.description: How ‘That Perfect Day’ Turns a Childhood Memory Into a Moving Portrait of Class and Parenthood ‘That Perfect Day’ explores the first sting of class difference, the quiet strength of fathers, and the kindness that makes life beautiful.

item.title: A Homegrown Guide to India’s Most Essential Regional Chillies
item.description: 7 Indian Chillies Every Home Cook Should Know Chillies aren’t native to India — they arrived via Portuguese traders in the 1500s. Today, they define our cuisine. Here are 7 iconic Indian chillies that belong in your pantry.

item.title: Monsoon Colour Lab Is Reviving India’s Analogue Film Infrastructure
item.description: Monsoon Colour Lab is restoring access to Super 8, 16mm, and 35mm film processing in India. Building on the legacy of Filmlab India, the lab opens amid a global revival of analogue media driven by young artists returning to physical formats.

item.title: At 'Tideline', Kochi Is Served In Courses, As A Means Of Documenting A City In Motion
item.description: How Tideline Is Using Food Unlock Kochi’s Untold Stories Tideline invites diners to listen and reflect as Kochi’s cultural histories unfold course by course.

item.title: Pashma’s Limited-Run Collection Is Made From Hundreds Of Cigarette Filters
item.description: Pakistani Brand Pashma Turns Discarded Cigarette Filters Into Bio-Based Vegan Leather Pashma’s material practice operates at the intersection of fashion, material research and environmental provocation.

item.title: Beedi Wars: How The Humble Beedi Sparked Decades Of Bloody Conflict In Kerala & Karnataka
item.description: Beedi Wars: How the Humble Beedi Sparked Decades of Bloody Conflict Across Kerala and Karnataka Conflict over the coastal cottage industry across North Kerala and Coastal Karnataka reshaped labour, politics, and everyday life, fueling cycles of blood-soaked revenge

item.title: The Face Of A Film: The Creative Chaos Of Three Homegrown Poster Designers
item.description: The Face Of A Film: The Creative Chaos Of Three Homegrown Poster Designers Homegrown speaks to Raj Khatri, Vinci Raj & Jahan Singh Bakshi about their practice in film poster design in Indian cinema.
